Supreme Court rejects request to intervene in CA election case
The US supreme court on Monday quickly rejected the Trump administration’s request to force California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump’s administration claims are noncitizens, the Associated Press reports.
The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. The decision came just hours after the administration asked the supreme court to intervene.
The ruling was the latest judicial rebuke in the face of a wave of unprecedented efforts from the Trump administration to intervene in the elections process of multiple states. The midterm elections are expected to bring nationwide victories for Democrats and impose more Congressional checks on Trump’s power.
In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters’ citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.
The high court did not detail its reasoning for rejecting the Trump administration’s request, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump’s push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.
Abdul El-Sayed mocked officials in the Trump administration during his final rally of his Michigan senate campaign, an event with the rapper Common at the Majestic Theater downtown Detroit, in front of over a thousand supporters.
On Trump, who make several Islamophobic remarks about El-Sayed today, and who keeps calling him “Mohammed,” he said: “Donald Trump can’t seem to remember what my name is, despite his incredibly high score on his cognitive test.”
He called vice president JD Vance “JV Dance.”
On health secretary Robert F Kennedy, who recently came to Michigan and disparaged the accomplishments of the Arab world, El-Sayed said: “His only expertise is that he understands what it means to have zero scientific contributions.”
“I’m like, habibi, listen, at the end of the day, I got two doctorates, you got none.”
“We beat their 70 million in the primary, they might as well have set their money on fire,” El Sayed said. “And we’re going to beat their 250 million in the general. Go ahead and set your money on fire.”
US envoy Steve Witkoff said the United States will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss ending Moscow’s war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation, Reuters reports.
US negotiators have been seeking a breakthrough in the long-running conflict before the winter sets in. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.
It’s worth noting just what a bureaucratic nightmare it would have been if the supreme court had sided with the Trump administration’s request that the court order California to identify and set aside 20,000 ballots that it claimed were potentially submitted by noncitizens.
As the Associated Press notes, voting has been underway in California, a largely Democratic state, since early October. All of the state’s roughly 23 million registered voters are mailed a ballot. Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. California election officials have said that finding and setting aside the challenged ballots now would be logistically impossible.
California officials are celebrating the Supreme Court ruling. Governor Gavin Newsom called the Trump administration’s attempts to intervene in the state’s election a “baseless attack.”
“After repeatedly losing in the lower courts, the highest court in the land firmly slapped down the Trump DOJ’s baseless attack on California’s electoral process — not even entertaining it,” Newsom said in a statement. “The third branch of government did its job, and that should be a welcome sight for all Americans given the disgusting and dangerous attacks on our democracy by the federal government. Tomorrow, Californians can feel secure in knowing the state will carry out a free and fair election — just as we’ve always done.”
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said state officials “will remain vigilant and keep fighting back against federal efforts to undermine our democracy.”
“Courts have now rejected the Trump Administration’s attempts to interfere in California’s elections not once, not twice, not three times, but four times — from the district court to the Ninth Circuit to the U.S. Supreme Court,” said Bonta in a statement. “This latest decision should put an end to the Administration’s attempt to disrupt California’s elections through emergency court orders.”
California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber said that Californians can now focus on voting.
“While this fight is not over yet, on the eve of Election Day, this means millions of Californians can focus on the most important task at hand — casting their ballot,” Weber said.
The Center for Election Innovation & Research (CEIR), a non-profit that focuses on restoring trust in the election system, celebrated the Supreme Court’s decision to reject the Trump administration’s request to intervene in the California election.
CEIR Executive Director David Becker said the Supreme Court reaffirmed “state sovereignty by swiftly rejecting the Justice Department’s illegal attempt to interfere with California’s election.”
The Trump administration had asked the Supreme Court to set aside thousands of mail-in ballots from California residents the administration claimed were non-citizens. State officials had previously said the list was full of errors.
“Every time the administration’s claims regarding noncitizen voters have been subjected to any sort of scrutiny, they have immediately fallen apart,” Becker said. “In California, Nevada, and every other state, the administration’s initial broad and vague claims have been found to be unsupported by evidence. In a hearing before a federal district judge just today, an attorney for the administration acknowledged the DHS lists of alleged noncitizens likely have a high error rate.
The Cook Political Report is now predicting that Michigan’s furiously contested senate race is more likely to be won by Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, after previously categorizing it as a “toss-up” race that was too close to call.
The shift comes amid last-minute outrage as sitting Democratic Michigan congresswoman Hayley Stevens endorsed El-Sayed’s Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, despite Stevens’ previous public attacks on Rogers when during a Democratic primary election that she lost. Stevens and El-Sayed’s contrasting policy views on Israelare seen as central to a “betrayal” that many Democrats are arguing may have cost the 43-year-old Stevens her career as a Democratic politician.
Judges across the country have repeatedly rebuked the Trump administration for its last-minute demand that California set aside 20,000 ballots that the administration claims it has evidence were cast by noncitizens —an unprecedented and possibly unconstitutional attempt to interfere with a state’s electoral process.
Today, the administration’s California gambit was rejected by two different courts in two separate cases in a matter of hours.
First, a federal judge in Washington ordered the Trump administration to stop demanding that California election officials set aside ballots from 20,000 people, writing, “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution’s Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone.”
Then, in a separate case, the supreme court swiftly rejected the Trump administration’s emergency request this morning that it intervene on the day before the election andforce California election officials to set aside the 20,000 mail ballots.
Democratic elections attorney Marc Elias called the supreme court ruling “A complete DEFEAT for Trump DOJ”noting that the court’s denial of the administration’s request came with “no noted dissents,” even from more conservative justices, and that the court “denied DOJ’s application about the California election without even asking for us to respond.”

Extreme weather is having an impact on voting and elections in the Southwest, as the National Weather Service estimated up to four inches of rain could fall through Monday across the Four Corners region — where New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and Utah meet — as the phenomenon stoked by warming Pacific waters known as El Niño disrupts weather patterns, the Associated Press reports.
Officials had warned of “potentially catastrophic” flooding in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town of about 2,000 nearly wiped out in 1911 when the San Juan River crested at approximately 17.8 feet (5.4 meters). The river reached 16.81 feet (5.1 meters) late Sunday night, flooding downtown streets, before receding Monday, the weather service said.
The Colorado Secretary of State’s office arranged alternative voting plans for evacuated or stranded residents of Pagosa Springs, Colorado. Other elections officials had urged voters to cast ballots before the storms hit.
Evacuations also were ordered along the San Juan River in New Mexico, which officials warned was still rising and could crest Tuesday through Wednesday. The village of Chama, New Mexico, was also evacuated and cut off by road closures.
In Michigan, where he is fighting for one of the country’s most fiercely contested US senate seats, Adbul El-Sayed and his supporters are focusing their closing message on the country’s healthcare crisis.
Speaking to reporters, El-Sayed, an epidemiologist who previously served as a county public health director, said that Medicaid coverage would be his number one priority if he his elected to the senate.
People who lose Medicaid coverage end up getting care in emergency rooms, where it is most expensive, and hospitals then push those costs into negotiations with insurers, El-Sayed said. And the cost ultimately lands on everyone, he added.
Earlier, Massachusetts senator Elizabeth Warren, who is campaigning in Michigan for El-Sayed, told his supporters in Royal Oak, a suburb of Detroit, that that higher wages and universal healthcare must be the heart of the Democratic agenda. “We want Medicare for All,” Warren said.
Former President Barack Obama has posted his personal endorsementof Democratic candidates running in four key swing states: Georgia, Ohio, Michigan and Maine.
His posts included photos of him campaigning with Democratic candidates at rallies in Georgia, Ohio, and Michigan, and a campaign video about Troy Jackson, the Democratic senate candidate in Maine.
Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass, a Democrat locked in an extremely close mayoral race with a challenger running to her left, Nithya Raman, has issued a statement condemning the Trump administration’s emergency appeal to the supreme court, asking for it to intervene in its attempt to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots that the administration has asserted were possibly submitted by noncitizens:
Donald Trump is asking the supreme court to intervene in the California ballot case the day before Election Day, after lower courts have already said no. This is a desperate attempt to scare people into staying home, and it’s a distraction from the real issues that matter to Angelenos and Californians.
It’s also an effort to make Americans doubt our elections, which are safe, secure, and run by dedicated election workers. Don’t fall for it.
digest_he:
בית המשפט העליון בארצות הברית דחה במהירות את בקשת הממשל של הנשיא דונלד טראמפ לחייב את מדינת קליפורניה להפריד ולא לספור אלפי פתקי הצבעה שנשלחו בדואר. ממשל טראמפ טען כי מדובר בקולות של אנשים שאינם אזרחי ארצות הברית, אך השופטים בחרו שלא להיענות לדרישת החירום ולא סיפקו נימוקים להחלטה כמקובל במקרים דומים. פסיקה זו מהווה דחייה משפטית נוספת לניסיונות הממשל להתערב בהליכי הבחירות במדינות השונות.

גורמים רשמיים בקליפורניה בירכו על החלטת בית המשפט והדגישו כי מערכת הבחירות במדינה תתנהל כפדתה באופן חופשי והוגן. המושל גווין ניוסום כינה את ניסיונות ההתערבות של ממשל טראמפ התקפה חסרת בסיס על התהליך הדמוקרטי. מנגד, הממשל המשיך להעלות טענות על הונאת בחירות רחבת היקף ולדרוש צעדים להגברת הפיקוח הפדרלי על ההצבעה במספר מדינות ברחבי ארצות הברית.

במקביל, המערכת הפוליטית בארצות הברית מתכוננת לבחירות האמצע, כאשר מועמדים שונים מקיימים עצרות בחחרות אחרונות. בין היתר, המועמד לסנאט במישיגן עבדול אל-סייד התייחס בעצרת בחירות לבחירות הקרובות ולביקורת שספג מיריביו הפוליטיים. במקביל, דיפלומטים אמריקאים ממשיכים במאמצים דיפלומטיים לקידום שיחות בין רוסיה לאוקראינה לקראת פגישות נוספות המתוכננות להתקיים באבו דאבי.
